guitar.notes: Kerry King's B.C. Rich Warlocks (and later signature B.C. Rich/ESP models) and Jeff Hanneman's similar B.C. Rich guitars are extremely well documented in thrash metal history.

tone.target: tight thrash rhythm with sharp palm-mute attack
tone.profile: tight thrash rhythm with sharp palm-mute attack
tone.summary: Gate 1 -> Green OD -> Distortion -> UK 800 -> UK Vintage 4x12 -> Guitar EQ 1 -> Chorus (off) -> Digital Delay -> Room -> Volume

blocks.purpose: Eliminate hum and excessive noise inherent in high-gain recording.
Provide aggressive pick attack and boost the signal into the high-gain distortion stage.
blocks.gap: The TS-style boost is best approximated by Green OD for mid-hump and aggression.

alternatives.reason: Slightly warmer, but still provides necessary boost.

blocks.purpose: Establish the core high-gain sound required for thrash metal and tight low end.
Simulate the Marshall-style high gain and punchy, aggressive tone.
Provide the necessary punch and definition associated with a classic Marshall-style 4x12 cabinet.
Achieve the required 'scooped mids' and enhance high-end bite for fast alternate picking.
Included for completeness, but kept inactive as per 'avoid' list (no chorus).
blocks.gap: The module is present but bypassed to meet the tone requirements.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic depth without muddying the tight rhythm tone.
blocks.gap: The delay is kept minimal to maintain focus on aggressive riffing.

blocks.purpose: Provide minimal, natural ambience to prevent the tone from sounding too sterile or dry.
blocks.gap: The mix is kept low to satisfy the 'minimal ambience' requirement.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for tighter low end and more defined attack.

proposals.reason: Enhance definition and tightness crucial for thrash palm-muting.
proposals.expectedGain: Tighter low end, better attack definition
